derived_from: fixtures/cb2 at d4febe6 (the frozen Qwen reading; untouched) by the recorded patch scratch/cb2n_patch.py; scratch/rederive.sh proves the tree re-derives exactly
profiles: profiles/<name>.profile, loaded by run/profile.sh (CB2_PROFILE, default qwen) THROUGH an immutable run state ($OUT/run_state.json: profile, upstream, resolved IPv4 addresses, first address, resolution time, model) written by the first loader call of a run and consumed unchanged by the network script, the proxy, both legs, the smokes and the cap test. qwen = the v3 reading unchanged: owned gateway 192.168.4.203, no key injection, the Mind on its local lane. nim (E.CB2-N) = upstream integrate.api.nvidia.com, its addresses resolved once (allowlisted EXCLUSIVELY: the network script fails closed if any other ACCEPT for the egress subnet survives), the key file (uid 10002, mode 0400) mounted read-only into the PROXY container only and injected as the Authorization header on every forward, placeholder keys in both work containers, one model for both systems (openai/gpt-oss-120b), the Mind via YM_PRIMARY_BRAIN=nim:<model> with all six YM_ROLE_* equal to it behind YM_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NIM (brain gate: env + boot log, fail closed). Key-leak scans hand the key FILE to grep as a pattern file (the key and its prefix never enter a variable, log or receipt); any hit in a work container's env, home, state, raw log or artifact disqualifies. Model identity: every model id tallied from SUCCESSFUL responses must equal the profile model, and at least one must exist, or the leg is disqualified (when not void). VOID = a TYPED proxy receipt showing an upstream 429/5xx on a model request or a transport/TLS failure (a failed upstream body read included; a client disconnect is counted separately and is not): infrastructure, never a disqualification by itself. A MISSING OR MALFORMED receipt is not that evidence: it is an independent disqualification. Cap evidence (a refusal, or accepted > cap) is independent too and stands whatever the upstream was doing; the Mind driver splits its own reasons the same way, independent (missing/malformed proxy receipt, a refusal, over-cap, a malformed ledger row) against dependent (the wall). A void leg preserves its first receipt and outputs as *_void1 and may be rerun exactly once, and only when it is PURELY void (void true, disqualified false, dq_independent false); a second void refuses. Other 4xx are the request errors of the caller: counted (upstream_client_errors), neither void nor rerun. A proxy that cannot come up writes a pre-invocation receipt with void true and disqualified false: nothing was graded. Egress policy lives in its own iptables chain CB2-EGRESS, flushed and rebuilt every run and jumped to from DOCKER-USER position 1 (established/related, one ACCEPT per resolved address on tcp/443, then DROP); the audit compares that chain rule for rule against the expected policy and fails closed on any difference, on a jump that is not first, or on any surviving DOCKER-USER rule naming the subnets. Each profile uses its own output root (/root/cb2n/out-qwen, /root/cb2n/out-nim), and every receipt carries the path and SHA-256 of the run state.
standing: three-task exploratory bakeoff, Mind vs Hermes only; NOT a superiority claim under competitive benchmark v1 (24 paired trials)
host: everything runs on the staging box 192.168.4.95 (Debian 13, Docker 26): both generation legs and all artifact execution inside containment; one host, no environment confound; wall time recorded per leg, never a ranking

containment.networks: net/cb2net.sh — cb2net 172.30.0.0/24 is --internal (no NAT, no egress): work containers (hermes, mind, check) live there and can reach only the run's proxy container. cb2egress 172.30.1.0/24 carries the proxy's second leg; the egress policy is NOT a set of loose DOCKER-USER rules but a dedicated chain CB2-EGRESS, flushed and rebuilt every run and reached by ONE jump inserted at DOCKER-USER position 1; its rules in order are ACCEPT established/related → 172.30.1.0/24, then one ACCEPT 172.30.1.0/24 → <address> tcp/443 per address in the run state (qwen: 192.168.4.203; nim: the resolved integrate.api.nvidia.com addresses), then DROP 172.30.1.0/24 → any. The audit fails closed unless the chain matches that policy rule for rule, the jump is the FIRST DOCKER-USER rule, and no other DOCKER-USER rule names either subnet; net/audit_probe.sh proves the last of those by seeding a stray rule and requiring the audit to reject it. Host services are blocked from BOTH bridges by interface-scoped INPUT rules (DROP, after established/related). All containers run --dns 127.0.0.1.
containment.probes: raw TCP connects, never HTTP fetches: net/probe_work.py (inside cb2net) must print 'proxy-tcp ok / gateway-tcp blocked / internet-tcp blocked / host-ssh-tcp blocked / host-http-tcp blocked / dns blocked'; net/probe_proxy.py (inside the proxy) must print 'gateway-tls-verified ok / internet-tcp blocked / host-ssh-tcp blocked / host-http-tcp blocked / dns blocked' (a hostname-VERIFIED TLS handshake, CERT_REQUIRED + check_hostname); the proxy's own startup handshake is recorded as tls_hostname_verified. The script exits non-zero otherwise.
containment.proxy: proxy/proxy.py (image cb2n-proxy, stdlib, uid 10002, read-only, limits): ONE per leg run; forwards every request verbatim (streaming included) to the run state's upstream by hostname (qwen: aig.mycluster.cyou at 192.168.4.203; nim: integrate.api.nvidia.com at its resolved address, Authorization injected from the proxy-only key file) over hostname-verified TLS; counts MODEL requests — EVERY POST except the single observed metadata probe POST /api/show (Hermes's model-info lookup); GETs are metadata; every path is tallied in by_path, so an unlisted inference path can never bypass the cap — and answers 429 from model request 9 — the cap holds BEFORE the ninth request reaches the model; writes counts to /count/requests.json after every request (an independent request receipt for both systems).
containment.hermes: image cb2-hermes (docker/hermes.Dockerfile: python:3.13-slim + the git archive of the pinned commit; uid 10001), --network cb2net --read-only --tmpfs /tmp, writable mounts: /work and a fresh per-task HERMES_HOME; --memory 4g --cpus 4 --pids-limit 512; base_url = the run's proxy
containment.mind: image cb2-mind (docker/mind.Dockerfile: debian:trixie-slim + libssl3 zlib zstd python3; uid 10003) with /opt/yantrik-mind/mind-core bind-mounted READ-ONLY (sha256 + provenance in the receipt), --network cb2net --read-only --tmpfs /tmp, a fresh state volume per task (YM_DB, YM_WEB_DIR), lane by profile — qwen: YM_LOCAL_OLLAMA_URL = the run's proxy, YM_PRIVATE_PROVIDERS=YM_HOUSEHOLD_PROVIDERS=ollama-local; nim: YM_PRIMARY_BRAIN=nim:<model> and all six YM_ROLE_* = the same spec behind YM_PROVIDER_BASE_URL_NIM = the run's proxy, placeholder NVIDIA_API_KEY=none, no local lane, the brain gate enforced from the container env and the boot log — no other provider key in either lane, no Telegram, no coder, DMN/proactive/patterns/home-watch off; the driver runs INSIDE the container (console API is loopback there); the state volume is removed after a counts-only teardown receipt
containment.checks: image cb2-check (playwright:v1.62.1-noble + pytest 8.3.5), --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp, a WRITABLE COPY of the artifact at /work, --memory 2g --cpus 2 --pids-limit 256, 300 s; every artifact is executed only there

mind.binary: the deployed staging mind-core, ledger tip at run time (sha256 + provenance in the receipt)
mind.invocation: one POST /api/agent {name, task} through the paired console inside the container; the delegate router chooses the executor
mind.known_limit: the coder needs an API key this scratch instance does not have, so the executors present are `page` and `research`. Since E.PORT1-B a brief the classifier calls `code` is NOT refused: the deterministic floor is constrained to the executors that exist, so it runs on `page`. The router may still refine the kind within its budget, so the receipt records the kind the job actually ran as, and a leg that produced no artifact because it was routed to `research` is a routing outcome rather than a build failure.

model.endpoint: reached only through the run's proxy
model.rule: the only model either system can reach — enforced by the network and the proxy, not by configuration; identical for both systems within a reading, checked from the successful responses' model ids

caps.sequential_runs: one leg at a time: every leg refuses to start while any container is attached to cb2net or cb2egress, so no stale or cross-run proxy is reachable
caps.proxy_start: fail-closed and PRE-INVOCATION: the leg aborts with a receipt of status proxy-not-ready, void true and disqualified false (nothing was graded, and the one declared rerun applies) unless the proxy started, took its fixed address, wrote a clean receipt (0 requests, 0 upstream errors, tls_hostname_verified true) and answers on its listener
caps.invalidation: Three classifications with a PRECEDENCE, not three disjoint buckets: an independent violation and an infrastructure void can hold at once, and the violation still disqualifies. INDEPENDENT violations disqualify unconditionally: an untyped or missing proxy receipt (receipt_valid false), a refusal or accepted > cap in that receipt, more calls than the cap in the own log of the agent, a download or install line, a key-leak hit, a symlink or special filesystem node, a failed capture, a failed brain gate, and the independent reasons the Mind driver reports (missing or malformed proxy receipt, a refusal seen, accepted > cap, a malformed ledger row). VOID (infrastructure, not the agent): a typed receipt showing an upstream 429/5xx on a model request or a transport/TLS failure, and a proxy that could not start at all (pre-invocation: void true, disqualified false, nothing graded). A void SUPPRESSES ONLY the dependent class and never rescues an independent violation. DEPENDENT violations disqualify only when the leg is not void: a non-zero exit including the wall, the agreement checks on the proxy receipt (1 <= accepted <= cap, refused 0, tls_hostname_verified true, accepted == the calls in the own log of the agent), and model identity.
caps.enforcement: the proxy refuses request 9 with 429 for BOTH systems (hard, before the model). Hermes additionally runs with agent.max_turns 8 and its receipt fails closed on a missing session id or log. The Mind driver stops at done/failed, at the first refusal, or at 1800 s with deadline-bounded waits (the parent stops the container right after the receipt) and reads the closed-schema ledger rows (v1, verdict served|failed|refused, attempts:<n>; ANY malformed row disqualifies) beside the proxy's count.
caps.manual_edits: none — artifact directories are made read-only at exit/done and tree-hashed immediately with a 60 s bound; cleanup is guaranteed by traps; the Mind capture takes files created OR content-changed since a sha256 baseline; symlinks and special filesystem nodes are never opened or hashed and disqualify
caps.downloads_installs: impossible by network (internal network, no DNS, proxy forwards only to the run state's upstream); any transcript line matching pip/npm/apt/curl/wget disqualifies anyway
caps.artifact_execution: only inside cb2-check with --network none, on a writable copy; the source tree is validated before copying and any symlink or special filesystem node is rejected

briefs.contracts: vendor-neutral store/render/CLI contracts appended to each brief (identical text to both systems)
briefs.sha256: receipts/briefs.sha256 — verifiable from the fixture root with `sha256sum -c receipts/briefs.sha256`

seed.semantics: 20 leads, UTC calendar days, 14 bins ending on the UTC date of the newest lead (2026-09-02) inclusive, every bin present; recent = 5 names newest first
seed.placement: the T1 checker writes the seed to data/leads.json in the writable copy before both the form check (expects exactly total+1 after submit) and the dashboard check (seed re-installed pristine)

checks.T1: checks/check_web.mjs t1 — run.sh present; site up on 8123; loads with 0 console errors and 0 non-loopback requests; relative links resolve; form#cb2-lead-form present; submit appends EXACTLY one record; the record equals the submitted fields with exactly the six contract keys and an ISO-8601 UTC created_at; /dashboard embeds script#cb2-dashboard whose total, per_day (14 exact keys and counts) and recent (5 names, order) equal seed/expected.json
checks.T2: checks/check_web.mjs t2 — loads with 0 console errors and 0 non-loopback requests; relative links resolve; section#projects has ≥4 article; section#writing has ≥3 article; section#contact has a mailto: link or a form
checks.T3: checks/check_t3.py — tracker.py present; test_*.py present and `python -m pytest -q` passes; on a fresh store: add→'added #1', add→'added #2', list = two exact lines, done 1→'done #1', list shows [x], today = the open task added today, tasks.json is a two-item array; every command its own process
checks.verdicts: counts and booleans only (stdout → verdict.json); every text excerpt (console messages, command output, errors) goes to a separate excerpts file that never enters a receipt
checks.static_server: the checker's static server refuses any path resolving above the artifact root
checks.live_proof_before_approval: clean-network migration with inspect fields; exact TCP probes both sides; a 9-POST cap test yielding accepted 8 / refused 1 / attempted 9 with upstream_errors 0 and tls true; a no-model Mind boot + pair smoke; a Hermes smoke through the proxy; the six exact self-tests — counts, hashes and statuses only
checks.selftest: selftest/selftest.sh — six checker fixtures (t1/t2/t3 × pass/fail), plus a special-node safety probe and selftest/verdict_cases.py (the Mind leg's disqualification rule, driven through every classification: clean, no proxy receipt, absent spend log, malformed ledger row, cap refusal, over-cap, accounting disagreement, zero model requests, the wall, and a retry that agrees because attempts and not rows are compared); each fixture must produce a verdict whose failed-check set equals the expected set EXACTLY (an infrastructure failure or a missing verdict is a self-test failure, never a pass), and the safety probe must prove a FIFO is counted without blocking and rejected before checker copy; results are sent to the reviewer before any graded run

output_dir_contract.mind: RESULT.md (the job's result text, the declared output) plus every file the job added under the scratch web dir, copied out of the state volume
output_dir_contract.tree_hash: tools/tree_hash.py — SHA-256 over sorted (relative path, bytes); excludes .git, __pycache__, node_modules, .pytest_cache, .venv, *.pyc, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db; counts but never opens symlinks or special filesystem nodes

receipts: run receipts carry counts, ids, hashes (artifact tree, binary, archive), image ids, timings and statuses only; the Mind receipt carries accounting_agrees beside ledger_attempts and proxy_accepted, so the agreement this manifest requires of BOTH systems is visible in the receipt and not merely asserted (it was implemented on the Hermes leg alone until an adversarial review found it missing); raw stdout/boot/driver logs and checker excerpts live under out/raw and never enter a receipt or verdict

cost.both: the proxy's model_requests per run (the same meter for both systems) and, when the upstream reports usage, its prompt/completion token counts summed over successful responses
cost.mind: ledger requests/attempts from the closed-schema rows; tokens absent
cost.hermes: API calls and provider-reported in/out tokens from its session log
cost.comparable: proxy model requests; tokens reported for Hermes with the mind's stated absent; wall recorded, not ranked

viewer_test: Pranab, blind: per task the two artifacts as A/B (map held by Codex outside the repo), fifteen seconds each, a forced pick; unsealed only after the pick is on the ledger
kill: a label unsealed before the pick
a check softened after a failure
a run on the live mind.db
any run that reached the internet, a host service, or installed anything
any run with proxy model_requests > 8 or over 1800 s
any malformed ledger row on the Mind side
a self-test whose failed-check set differs from the expected set at run time
the real key readable from any work container (a key-leak hit anywhere)
a successful response whose model id differs from the profile model
a model differing between the two systems within a reading
a NIM request before direct spend authorization from Pranab
